First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{{k}^{2}+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{k})+C
$$

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{\infty }\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{2}^{a}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{2}^{a}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{2}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]}_{2}^{a} \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡1) \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})]-\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/042ad2450306552d9d5a7e4219d15547ad7104601b7ce6350a64193981de0de7.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{\infty }\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{a}{2})]-\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
